name: Autofill and autocomplete tokens
plain: Form fields can ask the browser to fill saved name, email, phone, address and birthday.
meaning: Browser autofill puts personal data into inputs. Pages see it only after fill (often after user interaction on Chrome).

access.prompt_ui: Autofill dropdown; some sites need a click before values are readable
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Form fields can ask the browser to fill saved name, email, phone, address and birthday.

fields.name: cc-name, cc-number, cc-exp, cc-csc
fields.range: Chrome fills cards after confirmation; csc needs extra step

limits.headline: Can ask your browser to fill saved name, email, phone and address
limits.user_action: You tap a form field and choose a suggestion, or click first on some sites.
can: Fill name, email, phone, address and birthday from your saved details
Fill the fields it marks with the right label
Offer them as soon as you tap a field
cannot: See saved details before you pick them, on most browsers
Fill fields in a hidden form without your tap in most cases
limits.reach_label: What you pick at each form

story.what_it_is: Forms can ask your browser to fill name, email, phone, address and more.

marketing.name: autocomplete attribute
marketing.pitch: MDN says the attribute tells browsers what kind of data a form field wants, so they can autofill it.

story.for_you: You tap one form field, pick your saved info, and many fields fill at once. Some hidden fields can fill too, so check what you share.
story.for_makers: Makers add the right labels so your browser can fill signup and checkout forms. It lifts signups, but hidden fields can collect more than you meant to share.

use_cases.example: A checkout form fills name, address and phone in one tap.
A signup page fills your email and birthday.
A booking form fills passenger details.
A lead form fills fields for you, and you send more info than you thought.
A hidden field on a form collects phone or address that you never saw.
A loan form fills name and address, but you review the rest.

technical_bounds: Hidden fields can be filled by some autofill; browsers mitigate
Not a read API: the site only sees what the form posts

abuse: Harvesting hidden field autofill (known abuse by ad scripts)

history.change: autocomplete tokens defined in the HTML spec (autofill honoured earlier)
